title: Smriti Mandhana Becomes All-Time Highest Run-Scorer in Women's International Cricket
excerpt: The Indian opener surpassed Mithali Raj's 10,868-run mark with a record-breaking 124 off 64 balls against Hong Kong at the Women's T20 Asia Cup in Dubai.
body:
• Smriti Mandhana surpassed Mithali Raj's 10,868 career runs to become the all-time highest run-scorer in women's international cricket with 10,880 runs across all formats.
  • Her 124 off 64 balls against Hong Kong set a new record for the highest individual score in Women's T20 Asia Cup history, surpassing Chamari Athapaththu's unbeaten 119.
  • The century was Mandhana's 18th across formats, making her the batter with the most international centuries in women's cricket, passing Meg Lanning and Laura Wolvaardt.
  • India crushed Hong Kong by 137 runs in their Group A match in Dubai, posting 193-5 before bowling out their opponents for 56.

Smriti Mandhana etched her name into cricket history on Thursday, becoming the all-time leading run-scorer in women's international cricket during India's Women's T20 Asia Cup clash against Hong Kong in Dubai.

The 30-year-old left-hander smashed 124 off just 64 deliveries — an innings laced with 14 fours and seven sixes at a staggering strike rate of 193.55 — to power India to 193-5 in their Group A encounter. India then bowled Hong Kong out for 56, winning by 137 runs.

A Record Long in the Making

By the time she was dismissed in the final over of the innings, Mandhana's career tally had moved to 10,880 runs across Tests, ODIs and T20Is, surpassing former India captain Mithali Raj's mark of 10,868 runs accumulated over 333 international innings. Mandhana reached the landmark in 303 innings — a full 30 fewer than Raj needed.

The all-time top five in women's international cricket now reads: Mandhana (10,880), Raj (10,868), New Zealand's Suzie Bates (10,740), England's Charlotte Edwards (10,273) and West Indies's Stafanie Taylor (10,007).

The century was also Mandhana's 18th across all formats, taking her past Australia's Meg Lanning and South Africa's Laura Wolvaardt — both on 17 — for the most centuries in women's international cricket.

"Mithali has been such a legend and a role model. We've all grown up watching her bat, so to go past in the tally of runs is something that I'd definitely not imagined to do."

— Smriti Mandhana, post-match press conference

Praise From the Record Holder She Displaced

Raj, who retired in 2022 after a career spanning over two decades, responded on X with a message of congratulations.

"Well deserved," Raj wrote. "I've watched you grow from a young player into one of the finest batters India has produced. To see you go past my record and become the highest run-scorer in international cricket is a moment I'm genuinely proud of. Here's to many more runs and milestones."

Mandhana's Asia Cup Dominance

The 124 also displaced Sri Lanka's Chamari Athapaththu's unbeaten 119 against Malaysia in Dambulla in 2024 as the highest individual score in Women's T20 Asia Cup history. It was Mandhana's second T20I century, following her 112 against England in 2025, making her just the second Indian woman alongside Harmanpreet Kaur to score multiple T20I hundreds.

Mandhana, who made her India debut in 2013 as a 16-year-old, has compiled 788 runs in Tests at an average of 52.53, 5,411 ODI runs at 47.88, and 4,681 T20I runs at a strike rate of 126.55. She became the first Indian woman to score a century in all three formats last year.

What's Next

India have already secured their place in the Asia Cup semifinals. Mandhana and her teammates next face arch-rivals Pakistan on Saturday in their final Group A fixture at the Dubai International Stadium, where the vice-captain could become only the fifth player in women's cricket history to reach 11,000 international runs.
